source.title: H-CoT: Hijacking the Chain-of-Thought Safety Reasoning Mechanism to Jailbreak Large Reasoning Models, Including OpenAI o1/o3, DeepSeek-R1, and Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking
source.authors: Martin Kuo; Jian-Yi Zhang; Aolin Ding; Qin-Si Wang; Louis DiValentin; Yujia Bao; Wei Wei; Hai Li; Yiran Chen

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether a prompt-based attack that inserts mocked execution-phase reasoning can bypass safety refusals. This bears on the bypass claim, but it is a different intervention from compliant-opening prefills, fine-tuning, or token-position KL measurement.
record.gate_note: The study reports attack success rates and harmfulness ratings for H-CoT and comparison attacks, plus results without H-CoT for DeepSeek-R1 and Gemini. It does not test fine-tuning, aligned-versus-base KL by response position, safety localization in weights, or a safety-deepening intervention. The cited fine-tuning study is not a result of this paper. Table 1 also reports results by crime category; those category-specific values are not extracted here because the flattened layout makes reliable model/category assignment unclear.
record.test_reason: The study reports refusal-bypass rates on five reasoning models when mocked execution-phase reasoning is inserted around the harmful query. This is a prompt-side analogue of skipping past the refusal opening, tested in a new setting (large reasoning models), so it bears on V4. It is not a compliant assistant-turn prefill, an optimized suffix or a decoding change. The only link to the original sources is that Qi et al. is cited for the harmfulness judge.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that H-CoT, by injecting mocked execution-phase thoughts, drives refusal on reasoning models from about 98% to under 2%. They add that DeepSeek-R1 and Gemini barely refuse even without attack, and that o1's safety weakened after updates. They recommend hiding safety reasoning, separating CoT-style prompt content from the core request, and improving safety-reasoning training. They also report that explicit fake compliance justifications fail on o1.
record.recipe_differences: The intervention is prompt-based insertion of mocked execution-phase reasoning, not fine-tuning or token-prefill testing.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report lower H-CoT results for o3-mini than o1 in some category-level comparisons and suggest model-specific thought traces may improve effectiveness. They also report temporal-version and proxy-IP differences for o1, but the corresponding figure-only values are not extracted as rows.

fits_no_version.finding: o1 refusal on the benchmark fell between the January and February versions, and varied with proxy IP address (Figure 3, values not extracted).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deployed model updates and request geolocation change refusal rates on harmful educational-framed requests.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The benchmark contains 50 queries; testing used 10 attempts per query for o1 and o3-mini, 5 for o1-pro, DeepSeek-R1, and Gemini. Some findings rely on product web interfaces and changing model versions or proxy conditions. Category-specific table values are flattened in the supplied text, and temporal/geolocation results are presented in a figure without extractable numerical values.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 and Table 2 category-specific scores are not extracted because the supplied flattened table layout does not support reliable assignment of every value to a model, category, and metric. Figure 3 temporal-version and geolocation values are also not extracted because they are figure-only in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Assistant-turn prefilling of a compliant start, optimized adversarial suffixes such as GCG, and decoding changes. No per-position analysis of where refusal is decided.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
The causes of shallowness are discussed only informally, through an information-theoretic analogy.

missing.what: Failure of the altered-justification (T_J altered) attack on o1: the model kept refusing. This is qualitative and no numbers are given.
Category-level ASR/HR for H-CoT versus baseline, for example o1 TCI 75.0 and o3-mini SH 85.0, the lowest H-CoT categories.
H-CoT ASR across o1 versions and proxy IPs.

record.verdict_notes: Classification as a V4 test is loose. H-CoT inserts reasoning text in the user turn, not an assistant-turn prefill, so it is treated as T3 (new setting). The authors say o3-mini H-CoT results are 'relatively lower than o1', but the AVG values (98.0 vs 94.6) contradict this. The flattened Table 1 makes the o1-pro/o3-mini AVG column assignment uncertain, though the assignment used is consistent with the text. There is no uncertainty reporting, the benchmark has 50 queries, and testing used web UIs.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on benign or ordinary instruction data.
Tests H-CoT insertion of mocked execution reasoning, not compliant-opening prefills, optimized adversarial suffixes as a distinct method, or decoding changes.
No weight, parameter, or rank localization experiment.
The paper proposes explanations for H-CoT vulnerability but does not test whether training data or objective causes safety to be shallow.
No intervention that deepens safety across response positions, or evaluation of whether such an intervention holds up.

relationships.condition: o1 given an altered justification-phase text claiming compliance (with or without T_E)
relationships.reason: Text, no row: authors say this naive manipulation 'consistently refuses'. Asserting compliance does not bypass refusal; only skipping straight to execution-style reasoning does.
relationships.display_finding: The authors report that o1 consistently refused under this naive manipulation. Only skipping straight to execution-style reasoning bypassed refusal.
